request: Insert screws to both holes to be able to fix tool on the table

actions.operation: Insert/place screw fasteners into existing holes

parameters.assumed_hole_type: base mounting through-holes (vertical axis along Y) in base mounting foot
parameters.assumed_nominal_screw_size_basis: Hole wall radius in model.json is R≈7.5 => Ø≈15 mm; typical clearance suggests M14-class fastener (final standard to be confirmed)
parameters.insertion_direction_assumption: From base top face downwards toward the table (along -Y), so the screw heads remain accessible above the table

actions.target: both holes (base mounting holes in the base foot used to fasten the bracket/tool to the table)
actions.relational_constraint: Each screw axis concentric with its respective base mounting hole axis (hole wall faces FACE 0 and FACE 1); screw head underside coincident/offset to the base top face (FACE 57) as the bearing surface; shank passes through until the tip exits the underside (FACE 59) and continues into the table/nut/T-slot (external mate not in this model).
actions.unresolved_reference: Screw standard/type (hex socket cap, hex head, countersunk, etc.); exact nominal diameter and fit (clearance vs close); required screw length (depends on table thickness and engagement/nut/T-slot); whether washers are required; whether the table side uses tapped holes, through-holes with nuts, or T-slot nuts; whether the screw head should be flush (would require adding counterbore/countersink features to the base which are not present).
steps: Do not modify bracket solid geometry: the requested change is an assembly/fastener insertion interacting with existing mounting holes in Section SEC01 (Base mounting foot).

Identify the two vertical mounting through-holes in the base foot by selecting their cylindrical wall faces: left mounting hole wall face_code 0009 (Brep FACE 1) and right mounting hole wall face_code 0010 (Brep FACE 0). These define the hole axes (along Y) and diameters (R≈7.5).

Create/insert two screw components (Fastener_1, Fastener_2) from the CAD fastener library. Set the nominal thread size tentatively to match the clearance hole (approx. M14 if Ø≈15 is confirmed) and set head style per shop standard (to be confirmed).

For Fastener_1: apply an Axis Concentric (Mate: Concentric) constraint between the screw shank cylinder axis and the left hole cylinder (face_code 0009 / FACE 1). This locks radial position and aligns the screw along the hole axis.

For Fastener_1: apply a Planar Coincident (Mate: Coincident) constraint between the underside of the screw head (or washer underside if used) and the base top interface plane (face_code 0008 / FACE 57). If the design intent is clamp-down onto the table with head on top, set a small offset = 0 (or washer thickness as needed).

For Fastener_1: set the insertion direction so the screw points toward the table (along -Y) and verify the shank passes through the base and exits at the base underside mounting face (face_code 0000 / FACE 59) without interference.
Repeat the same constraints for Fastener_2 using the right hole cylinder (face_code 0010 / FACE 0) and the same head-bearing plane (face_code 0008 / FACE 57).

If a more explicit ‘fixed to table’ representation is required: add a simplified table plate component and mate the bracket base underside (face_code 0000 / FACE 59) coincident to the table top face; then mate screw tips into table tapped holes or into nut components (not present in current model).

Regenerate/solve assembly mates and confirm: both screws are coaxial with their respective holes, heads seat on the base top, and the bracket underside remains the intended contact surface to the table.

intention: Enable fastening (fixing) the tool to the table by using the two base mounting through-holes as the primary clamp-down interfaces, without altering the bracket geometry unless flush-head seating is later required.
